..
Issued at 259 AM EDT Sat Jul 25 2026

Current-Tonight...Hot & humid with L90s at the immediate coast and 
M90s (ISOLD U90s) esp into Osceola northward across the interior. 
Peak heat indices 102-107F (ISOLD to SCT 108-110F) with widespread 
Moderate to Major HeatRisk (ISOLD Extreme) areawide. Have hoisted a 
Heat Advisory for Volusia, Lake, Seminole, Orange, and Brevard 
counties for 12pm-7pm today.

Deep moisture continues to surge into ECFL. ISOLD to WDLY SCT 
showers across the adjacent coastal waters may occasionally push 
onto the coast (esp Cape southward) this morning before gradually 
dissipating. Mid-level high pressure ridging will persist across 
the central FL peninsula with 500 mb temps only - 5.0C to -5.5C 
with no notable shortwave impulses nearby. Surface heating, 
moisture, and late day/evening boundary collisions will be the 
catalysts for diurnal convection later today. Light/variable 
morning winds will turn onshore as the ECSB pushes inland this 
afternoon with strongest collisions across the central FL 
peninsula. Storm steering light/variable (under 5 mph) so erratic 
movement may take place from stronger collisions and heavy 
rainfall will be a primary threat due to slow/inconsistent 
movement of cells. Lightning strikes, and locally gusty winds will
also be in play. Will pay close attention in localized torrential
downpours as quick 1-3" precip totals (perhaps 4") may occur. 
PoPs 20-50% with highest chances likely from near Orlando
southward and perhaps only 10-20% for much of Volusia County.  
Activity will wind down thru mid-late evening. Warm & muggy 
overnight with persistent lows in the 70s. 

Sun-Sun Night...Deep moisture (PWATs well above 2") take grip across 
ECFL areawide. A weak pressure gradient continues in place with 
light W/NW flow. Offshore flow is relatively deep, albeit light, and 
expect the ECSB to develop but it could be delayed with minimal 
movement inland during the afternoon. Greatest boundary collisions 
will be across the eastern peninsula late on this day with NWRLY 
steering flow 10-15 mph which will take activity to the coast and 
across the local coastal waters. Have capped PoPs at 70% areawide 
and the Weather Prediction Center has placed all of ECFL in a 
Marginal (5-14%) Excessive Rainfall Outlook. Heavy rainfall (2-4" 
locally) with localized minor/nuisance flooding will be a main 
impact from NMRS lightning storms. Lightning strikes and gusty 
winds 40-55 mph locally will also be possible. Embedded shortwave 
impulses in the 500 mb flow aloft will aid convection as mid-level 
ridging breaks down. 500 mb temps forecast -5.5C to -6.0C. 

Max temps will be in the L-M90s with peak heat indices approaching 
102-107F ahead of any sea breezes or precipitation. Will continue to 
monitor for Heat Advisory criteria (108-110F). Widespread Moderate 
to Major HeatRisk (ISOLD Extreme) conditions will continue to impact 
those without adequate cooling and hydration. Lows continue in the 
70s.

Mon-Fri...Weak high pressure ridging continues with associated ridge 
axis remaining south of ECFL thru this period. A weak frontal 
boundary remains forecast to drift south toward north FL near/past 
mid-week as very deep moisture (PWATs well in excess of 2")
continues to surge across the area. Offshore flow appears to 
dominate this week, with possible ECSB appearances on Mon/Tue, but
inland movement will be futile. The ECSB may be hard-pressed to 
develop at all Wed-Fri as low-level offshore flow increases. With 
mid/upper level high pressure concentrating further westward, 
troughiness will align across the eastern CONUS, thus allowing 
shortwave impulses to dive southward across the FL peninsula in 
the NW/N flow aloft which will aid in daily convection. NMRS
(60-70%) diurnal PoPs most days in the extended. Will likely 
need to focus on heavy rainfall potential each day on top of 
frequent lightning strikes and gusty winds with storms. 

No real break in sight with high temps (90-95F) and peak heat 
indices continuing to average 102-107F each afternoon ahead of sea 
breeze/storms. Will continue to monitor for the need for any Heat 
Advisories, as portions of ECFL could still see heat index values 
reach around 108-110F.
